turns.question: Where are streaming responses implemented, and which public API methods route into the streaming implementation?
turns.text:
Now let's look at the higher-level streaming helpers (`lib/`) that wrap `Stream` for chat completions, responses, and assistants, plus the resource methods that expose `.stream()` public APIs.Found it — found in `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts`. Let me view the actual public methods there.Now let me view the actual `create` and `stream` method bodies (lines ~62-230) precisely.Now let's find `Responses.stream()` and `Responses.parse()` with streaming, plus assistants `createAndStream`/`stream` methods.Now let's check the Assistants beta `runs.ts` and `threads.ts` streaming entry points, and `lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts` core, plus `helpers.md` to confirm documented public API surface.I now have a complete picture. Let me quickly check `ResponseStream.ts`'s `createResponse` to confirm it also bottoms out at `client.responses.create` → core `Stream`.I have enough evidence to answer completely.

## Streaming implementation

**Low-level transport** — `src/core/streaming.ts`
- `Stream<Item>` class implements `AsyncIterable<Item>`.
- `Stream.fromSSEResponse()` parses a raw `fetch` `Response` as Server-Sent Events (via `_iterSSEMessages`/`SSEDecoder`) into typed events.
- `Stream.fromReadableStream()` parses a newline-delimited JSON `ReadableStream` (used to rehydrate a stream from an HTTP proxy/webhook body).

**Routing point** — `src/internal/parse.ts`, function `defaultParseResponse()`:
```ts
if (props.options.stream) {
  ...
  if (props.options.__streamClass) {
    return props.options.__streamClass.fromSSEResponse(response, props.controller, client, ...);
  }
  return Stream.fromSSEResponse(response, props.controller, client, ...);
}
```
This is invoked from `src/core/api-promise.ts` (`APIPromise.parseResponse`, defaulting to `defaultParseResponse`) once the underlying `fetch` completes. So *every* resource `create`/`retrieve` call that sets `stream: true` on `FinalRequestOptions` ends up here, and the response becomes a `Stream<T>` (or a custom subclass if `__streamClass` is set).

**Higher-level convenience wrappers** (all built on top of `core/streaming.ts`, via `src/lib/EventStream.ts` base class):
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts` — `ChatCompletionStream` (event-emitting wrapper for Chat Completions streaming, accumulates deltas).
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.ts` — adds automatic tool-calling loop on top of `ChatCompletionStream`.
- `src/lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts` — `ResponseStream` (equivalent wrapper for the Responses API).
- `src/lib/AssistantStream.ts` — `AssistantStream` (Assistants/Runs API streaming, `beta.threads`/`beta.threads.runs`).
- `src/lib/AbstractChatCompletionRunner.ts` — shared base for chat runner classes (tool-calling + streaming/non-streaming).

## Public API methods that route into streaming

| Public method | File | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| `client.chat.completions.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:71-82` | sets `stream: body.stream ?? false` on the request options → returns `APIPromise<Stream<ChatCompletionChunk>>` via `defaultParseResponse` |
| `client.chat.completions.stream(params)` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:222-227` | calls `ChatCompletionStream.createChatCompletion(this._client, body, options)` |
| `client.chat.completions.runTools({stream:true,...})` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:~200-215` | dispatches to `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.runTools(...)` |
| `client.responses.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts:100-116` | same `stream:` passthrough → `APIPromise<Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.responses.retrieve(id, {stream:true})` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts:140-161` | same pattern (streaming a stored/in-progress response) |
| `client.responses.stream(params)` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts:202-206` | calls `ResponseStream.createResponse(this._client, body, options)` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.createAndStream(...)` | `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts:166-171` | calls `AssistantStream.createAssistantStream(...)` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.stream(...)` | `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts:233-234` | same `AssistantStream.createAssistantStream(...)` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.submitToolOutputsStream(...)` | `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts:295-300` | calls `AssistantStream.createToolAssistantStream(...)` |
| `client.beta.threads.createAndRunStream(...)` | `src/resources/beta/threads/threads.ts:183-184` | calls `AssistantStream.createThreadAssistantStream(...)` |

All paths ultimately bottom out in `Stream.fromSSEResponse` (`src/core/streaming.ts`), invoked from `defaultParseResponse` in `src/internal/parse.ts`, which is the single chokepoint where `options.stream`/`options.__streamClass` decides SSE parsing.

**Not verified:** I did not trace `client.post`/`client.get` in `src/client.ts` line-by-line to confirm exactly how `stream` flows from resource call into `FinalRequestOptions` before reaching `api-promise.ts` (only confirmed the option is passed and that `defaultParseResponse` reads `props.options.stream`). I also did not read `src/resources/realtime/*` or `src/realtime/*` (WebSocket-based Realtime API) in detail — that's a separate streaming mechanism (WebSocket, not SSE) and out of scope unless you want it included. I did not open `src/lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts` or `AssistantStream.ts` in full, only enough to confirm their static factory methods.

This library provides convenient access to the OpenAI REST API from TypeScript or JavaScript.

It is generated from our [OpenAPI specification](https://github.com/openai/openai-openapi) with [Stainless](https://stainlessapi.com/).

To learn how to use the OpenAI API, check out our [API Reference](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference) and [Documentation](https://platform.openai.com/docs).

## Installation

```sh
npm install openai
```

### Installation from JSR

```sh
deno add jsr:@openai/openai
npx jsr add @openai/openai
```

These commands will make the module importable from the `@openai/openai` scope. You can also [import directly from JSR](https://jsr.io/docs/using-packages#importing-with-jsr-specifiers) without an install step if you're using the Deno JavaScript runtime:

```ts
import OpenAI from 'jsr:@openai/openai';
```

README:
# OpenAI TypeScript and JavaScript API Library

[![NPM version](<https://img.shields.io/npm/v/openai.svg?label=npm%20(stable)>)](https://npmjs.org/package/openai) ![npm bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/openai) [![JSR Version](https://jsr.io/badges/@openai/openai)](https://jsr.io/@openai/openai)

This library provides convenient access to the OpenAI REST API from TypeScript or JavaScript.

It is generated from our [OpenAPI specification](https://github.com/openai/openai-openapi) with [Stainless](https://stainlessapi.com/).

To learn how to use the OpenAI API, check out our [API Reference](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference) and [Documentation](https://platform.openai.com/docs).

## Installation

```sh
npm install openai
```

### Installation from JSR

```sh
deno add jsr:@openai/openai
npx jsr add @openai/openai
```

These commands will make the module importable from the `@openai/openai` scope. You can also [import directly from JSR](https://jsr.io/docs/using-packages#importing-with-jsr-specifiers) without an install step if you're using the Deno JavaScript runtime:

```ts
import OpenAI from 'jsr:@openai/openai';
```

## Usage

The full API of this library can be found in [api.md file](api.md) along with many [code examples](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/tree/
